clusters.name: Divergent boundaries
clusters.fact: At divergent boundaries, plates move apart and rising mantle melts as pressure falls, supplying magma that forms new crust.

basaltic crust.text: The mafic oceanic crust produced as magma cools at a spreading center.

clusters.name: Subduction zones
clusters.fact: At a subduction zone, dense oceanic lithosphere bends beneath another plate, forming a trench, an inclined earthquake zone, and commonly a volcanic arc.

Wadati-Benioff zone.text: The dipping plane of earthquake foci that traces a descending slab.

accretionary wedge.text: Sediment scraped from the descending plate and piled onto the overriding plate.

clusters.name: Continental collision
clusters.fact: When two buoyant continental plates converge, neither readily sinks; the crust shortens, thickens, and rises into mountain belts and high plateaus.

suture zone.text: The deformed belt marking where two formerly separate continental blocks joined.

fold-and-thrust belt.text: A zone where compression folds rock layers and stacks them along thrust faults.

clusters.name: Transform boundaries
clusters.fact: At transform boundaries, plates slide horizontally past one another, concentrating lateral displacement along strike-slip fault zones without creating or consuming crust.

offset streams.text: Channels displaced sideways where repeated fault motion cuts across their courses.

linear valleys.text: Straight valleys produced where erosion follows fractured and sheared rock along a fault zone.

bridges.fact: Oceanic lithosphere links the two boundaries: it is created and carried away from spreading ridges, then bends downward and is recycled at subduction zones.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts directly involve magma creating volcanic rock or landforms?
lenses.explanation: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a volcanic spreading center; seafloor spreading adds magma that cools into new crust; basaltic crust is that volcanic product; and volcanic arcs form where subduction promotes melting beneath the overriding plate.
lenses.label: Volcanic activity

lenses.prompt: Which concepts explicitly identify a fault or a zone defined by earthquake activity?
lenses.explanation: The Wadati-Benioff zone is defined by its dipping plane of earthquake foci; the San Andreas Fault is an active plate-boundary fault; and strike-slip fault names the lateral fault type whose sudden slip produces earthquakes.
lenses.label: Earthquake activity
